To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

localized perfusion with an antagonist specific to α3β2 receptors resulted in reversible blockade of ganglonic transmission in the canine parasympathethetic ganglia, whereas an antagonist specific for α3β4 receptors had little effect on ganglionic transmission.
functional neuronal nACHRs in canine parasympathetics contain an α3/ β2 subunit interface.

functional ganglioneuronal transmission in canine intracardia ganglion in situ is mediated primarily by nicotinic acetyllycholine receptors containing an α-conotoxin MI-sensitive α3/β3 subunit interface, and that a smaller contribution is made by receptors containing an a-conotoxin M1-insensitive α7 subunit interface, but not by α-conotoxin AuB-sensitive α3/ β4 subunit interface.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of the subunit composition and molecular structure of neuronal nAChR subunits that form functional receptors in vivo in mammals.
the subunit composition and pharmacology of nicotinic acetyl choline receptors that mediate ganglioni transmission in the cardiac parasympathic nervous system in vivo.
the identification of the subunit composition and pharmacological properties of the functional nicotinic receptor in the canine intrathoracic parasympathetically innervated ganglion.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
functional ganglonic transmission is primarily mediated by receptors containing an interface between α3 and β2, but with a smaller contribution from receptors containing an interface with α7.
functional nAChR-mediated ganglionic transmission occurs in vivo at the canine intracar-diac parasympa-thetic ganglion and that it involves α3β2 nAChRs.
functional ganglonic nAChRs at this synapse contain α3, β2, α7, and β4 nicotinic receptor subunits.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
α-conotoxin AuIb is not specific for α3/β3/β4 receptors and that α7 receptors are not specific for α-conotoxin ImI.

functional nAChR channels in canine intracardic ganglionic transmission are primarily composed of α3β2 subunit interfaces, with a lesser contribution by α7 subunit interfaces, and that α3β4 subunit interfaces may not be required for function.
α3β2 and α3β4 receptors are the primary functional neuronal nACHRs in canine intracardial ganglia.
The main takeaway from our work is that
functional nAChR subtypes can be identified and characterized by using a physiologically relevant in vivo preparation.
the α3/β 2 nAChR is the predominant functional nAChR in the canine intraganglionic parasympathetics.
functional nAChR channels in the peripheral auton-omous nervous system are not simply a combination of all possible subunits, but instead are highly selective in the subunit combinations they form.
